This application coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER Case Diary is perused.
Learned counsel for the rival parties are heard.
This is the first application u/S.439 Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant was arrested on 21.03.2023 by Police Station- Gopalpur District- Shivpuri (M.P.) in connection with Crime No.08/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 342,
506 of IPC and Section 5(n)/6 of POCSO Act.

sentences.text: I n brief case of the prosecution is that on 18.03.2023 at 9:31 pm prosecutrix aged about 17 years alongwith her parents lodged an FIR at Police Station Gopalpur District Shivpuri against present applicant that she has studied upto 11th standard.
Her date of birth is 10.03.2006.
On 05.03.2023 in the evening at 6 pm, she was fetching water from the tap installed in the house of present applicant.
At that time, present applicant called her inside the room.

When she entered the room, present applicant closed the door and forcibly committed sexual intercourse with her and threatened the prosecutrix that if she told about the incident to anyone, he will kill her.
The present applicant is harassing the prosecutrix on regular basis.
After 15 days, she narrated the incident to her mother.
On her complaint, aforesaid offence was registered against the applicant.
She was sent for medical examination.
On medical examination, no abnormality was found on her body.
Applicant was arrested.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The applicant is in custody since 21.03.2022 and he is the permanent resident of District- Shivpuri (M.P.).
There is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
The applicant is ready to abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
With the aforesaid submissions, prayer for grant of bail is made.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for dismissal of the application.
Learned counsel for the complainant opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection by submitting that the FIR is not highly belated and the prosecutrix is minor.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case,
this Court is of the opinion that the application should be allowed and by allowing the application it is ordered that if applicant furnishes a cash security of Rs.25,000/- alongwith a personal bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, he should be released on bail.
He will present during trial before the trial Court on each and every date.
In case of any default, cash security of Rs.25,000/- shall be forfeited without giving any notice.
Application stands allowed and disposed of.
Copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DEEPAK KUMAR AGARWAL) JUDGE ojha Chandan Dhakad vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84436640/
